Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's fourth heading for the Julian 17 April, „Преп. Саватије и Зосим.“, with Преп. left off, which is the venerable the rank table reads out of it and which this folder's `types` and the site's own honorific carry. One rank word stands over the pair and belongs to neither name, and the heading gives him no epithet and no monastery — Solovki is in the body, and this corpus keeps it in the display name and in `office`. So the bare forename is left, and the Prologue's form is Зосим and not Зосима. Measured, and the reader's prediction was wrong: `corpus-gate.mjs` run without `--batch` lists `? "зосим" — zosimas-of-palestine, zosimas-of-solovki`, and `zosimas-of-palestine` already held this same bare Serbian form, Зосим and not Зосима, off its own Prologue heading. A deliberate fold, recorded in the run's findings.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 17ης Απριλίου — «Όσιος Ζωσιμάς»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 17 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and heads him «(; - 1478)». The day's line is bare, «Όσιος Ζωσιμάς», and it is the page that identifies him: «ο μεγάλος ασκητής του Ρωσικού Βορρά», founder of the coenobitic life on Solovki. The corpus holds eight others of this name — among them Zosimas of Palestine, Zosimas of Cilicia and the Zosimas kept on 24 January — and none of them is of Solovki. The page names Germanus, whom it says is honoured on 30 July, and Sabbatius on 27 September; Sabbatius has a folder here and Germanus has none. The page prints no couplet and no hymn.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 30.04.2026 (17. април ст. ст.) — „Преп. Саватије и Зосим.“

attestations.note: The day's fourth entry, an enumerated pair, on the same menologion day the Greek keeps him on. **The 1478 agrees exactly** with what the folder already holds off saint.gr, so no date was added and none changed. The entry is two sentences: that he and Sabbatius were the founders of the ascetic community on the Solovetsky island in the White Sea, and that many great saints were glorified in that community. **Sabbatius, the first name in the heading, took no row**: his `serbian` row is already `venerated`, on the Julian 27 September and off this same book, so the second day he is owed is a reading for the report and not a draft — `BRIEF-SERBIAN.md` §1 — and it is in the run's findings, unwritten. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
